articles.headline: Ranveer Singh Outpaces Ranbir Kapoor in Advance Ticket Sales as Dhurandhar 2 Holds the Throne
articles.dek: Advance booking figures reveal that Dhurandhar 2 maintains its commanding lead over Ramayana at the Indian box office, keeping its opening-day pre-sales record safe.

body.h: The Unprecedented Pre-Release Momentum of Dhurandhar 2
p: Ranveer Singh's upcoming feature has firmly established its dominance as an extraordinary theatrical phenomenon long before opening night. Built upon the tremendous momentum generated by its predecessor, the sequel commanded immense eagerness from audiences across the country.
This high level of enthusiasm directly translated into staggering pre-release ticket purchases at the Indian box office, setting a remarkably high standard for upcoming cinematic projects.

Ahead of its premiere, the action-heavy sequel shattered expectations by comfortably surpassing the fifty-crore milestone in gross advance collections for its first day, even when accounting for record paid previews.
Such formidable pre-sale numbers positioned the film as a towering benchmark that subsequent theatrical releases would find exceedingly difficult to challenge or eclipse.

body.h: Ramayana Enters the Box Office Race
p: Among the prominent challengers anticipated to threaten this ticket-sales record was the heavily anticipated project starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Yash.

Produced on an exceptionally grand scale and recognized as one of the most expensive Indian motion pictures ever made, the mythological epic carried extraordinarily high expectations from trade analysts and fans alike.

Despite immense initial curiosity surrounding the star-studded cast and its historical subject matter, recent ticketing data indicates that the film will likely fall short of the benchmark established by its rival.

Reports show that the epic has sold roughly 523 thousand tickets on BookMyShow two days prior to its premiere, whereas the competing sequel had already moved approximately 1.1 million passes at the exact same timeframe.
In terms of monetary value, the grand-scale epic has generated approximately 24 crore rupees through initial Day 1 pre-sales at the domestic box office.

Industry estimates project that its final advance figures will ultimately settle between 32 and 37 crore rupees, leaving it trailing significantly behind the 50-crore opening-day gross recorded by the Ranveer Singh starrer.
With the mythological contender failing to match these pre-release metrics, the extraordinary ticketing record set by the sequel appears secure through the year 2026.
The blockbuster outing highlights the unmatched commercial appeal and audience pull commanded by the franchise, further solidifying its status as a monumental success in modern cinema.

Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar 2 continues to maintain its box office supremacy by outperforming Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana in advance ticket bookings. While the ambitious epic led by Kapoor has generated substantial pre-release figures, it remains considerably behind the fifty-crore opening-day benchmark set by the Dhurandhar sequel.

facts: Dhurandhar 2 crossed the ₹50 crore mark in advance gross collections for Day 1.
Ramayana sold approximately 523K tickets on BookMyShow two days before release.
Dhurandhar 2 sold 1.1 million tickets at the same stage before release.
Ramayana grossed around ₹24 crore through Day 1 advance bookings at the Indian box office.
Ramayana's final pre-sales are expected to settle in the range of ₹32-37 crore.
Ramayana is headlined by Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash.

articles.headline: Namit Malhotra Confirms Ramayana Part 2 Postponed to 2028 and Hints at Possible Trilogy
articles.dek: Producer Namit Malhotra has announced that the sequel to Ramayana will now arrive in 2028 and suggested the narrative might expand into a three-part series.

p: Producer Namit Malhotra has officially stated that the second instalment of the ambitious project Ramayana will be pushed back from its initial 2027 release window. The upcoming film is now scheduled to debut in theatres in the year 2028.

The decision to shift the release timeline comes as the production team seeks additional time to refine the visual elements. According to the producer, the extra duration will ensure that the grand finale receives the same meticulous attention to detail as the opening instalment.

body.h: Global Scope and Dual Master Versions
p: While discussing the scale of the production with E! News, Malhotra explained that the feature was originally designed as an Indian story tailored for a worldwide audience. However, the international scope expanded significantly throughout the filming process.

To cater effectively to global viewers, the team developed two separate master cuts of the first film. The English presentation features an entirely distinct edit along with a rewritten script designed to offer a unique viewing experience overseas.

Malhotra emphasized that avoiding a rushed production schedule was a primary factor in postponing the sequel. The creators are determined not to get ahead of themselves while working on such a massive undertaking.

Giving the project an extra year will reportedly provide the necessary breathing room to craft a worthy conclusion. The team believes this extended window is essential to properly execute a cinematic experience of this magnitude.

In a separate conversation with Review Nation, the producer dropped hints that the overarching story might eventually be stretched into a trilogy. The epic was initially conceived as a three-part narrative before the filmmakers streamlined it into two parts.

Makers are currently keeping their options open regarding the narrative structure. Future decisions will largely depend on audience reception and feedback once the initial chapters are fully released to the public.

Creative adjustments for subsequent instalments will hinge on how the world responds to the unfolding narrative. The filmmakers remain open to adding or subtracting plot elements based on upcoming viewer analytics.

Director Nitesh Tiwari and the production crew hope to evaluate these audience reactions closely. Ideally, future iterations might avoid the need for completely separate language edits if audience feedback points toward a unified vision.

Helmed by director Nitesh Tiwari, the high-profile project boasts an ensemble cast featuring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sai Pallavi as Sita. Additionally, Sunny Deol portrays Lord Hanuman while Yash takes on the role of Ravana.

Backed financially by Yash and Namit Malhotra, the feature has been mounted on a staggering budget of four thousand crore rupees. This massive financial backing places it firmly among the most expensive cinematic endeavours in Indian film history.

The project recently held a high-profile premiere event in Los Angeles on October 28, drawing early praise from critics who drew comparisons to massive international franchises like Avatar and The Lord of the Rings.
With the first part arriving in theatres ahead of Diwali on November 5, audiences attending the premiere have already begun looking forward to the developments promised in the delayed sequel.
Producer Namit Malhotra has confirmed that Ramayana Part 2 will release in 2028 to allow for more production time and hinted that the story could become a trilogy based on audience reactions.
The high-budget project directed by Nitesh Tiwari features a star-studded cast and follows a grand international rollout for its first instalment.

Nitesh Tiwari is the director of the film.

articles.headline: Sam Fender Covers The Rolling Stones for John Lewis Christmas Campaign
articles.dek: The artist puts a unique spin on a 1969 classic for the holiday season, earning praise from rock royalty.

p: The annual festive commercial from John Lewis has officially made its debut, pairing a magical storyline with a prominent musical cover. This year's narrative centers on a grandmother named Gloria who struggles to find suitable holiday presents for her grandchildren before discovering fresh inspiration.

Guided by a talking wooden toy named Pickles, Gloria travels to London and builds a special space called a Gran Cave in her home. There, she shares joyful moments and dancing with her grandchildren Maggie and Freddie while music plays in the background.

For the soundtrack of the campaign, the retailer selected the legendary Rolling Stones track You Can't Always Get What You Want. Originally launched in 1969 as part of the studio album Let It Bleed, the song has been given a brand-new arrangement for the commercial.
The vocal duties for this fresh rendition were handled by Sam Fender. The collaboration brings a distinct emotional depth to the holiday spot through a carefully crafted musical backdrop.

To make the recording distinct, the performer enlisted local talent connected to his own background. He brought in children attending his former school, John Spence Community High School, to form a special choir.

In addition to the youthful voices, the arrangement features a robust brass section provided by the Easington Colliery Band. This collective effort adds layers of warmth and scale to the finished track.

The reworked version of the 1969 tune did not go unnoticed by its original creators. Mick Jagger expressed personal admiration for the project, noting that he appreciates the musician's prior body of work.
The veteran rock star shared positive thoughts on the new interpretation, giving the rendition his official endorsement. The track was originally co-written by Jagger alongside Keith Richards.
Listeners interested in owning physical copies of the song will have options available through retail and artist channels. The audio will be pressed onto seven-inch vinyl records and compact discs.
Proceeds generated from these physical sales are dedicated to charitable causes. Contributions will support Action for Children and the Teenage Cancer Trust.

The artist behind the holiday track has accumulated numerous accolades over the years. His previous achievements include five Brit Awards, two Ivor Novello Awards, and recognition with the Mercury Prize.
His prior output features major chart success, including a prominent collaboration with Olivia Dean that claimed top honors at the Brit Awards and broke records in British music history.

The collaboration places the singer into a long-standing tradition of notable musicians providing the soundtrack for holiday campaigns. Previous years have featured performances by artists such as Elton John, Lily Allen, Andrea Bocelli, and Labrinth.
These seasonal spots have historically become cultural touchstones, frequently driving massive public discussion around their musical choices as much as their visual storytelling.

Sam Fender has recorded a cover of The Rolling Stones track You Can't Always Get What You Want for the John Lewis holiday commercial, receiving praise from Mick Jagger. The release involves his former school choir and the Easington Colliery Band, with physical record sales raising funds for charitable organizations.

facts: Sam Fender covered You Can't Always Get What You Want for the John Lewis Christmas advert.
The song was originally released by The Rolling Stones in 1969 from their album Let It Bleed.
Mick Jagger praised the new cover version.
Profits from physical record sales will be donated to Action for Children and the Teenage Cancer Trust.
Sam Fender involved children from his old school, John Spence Community High School, and the Easington Colliery Band.

articles.headline: Ramayana Projected For Rs 160 Crore Opening Day As Global Pre-Sales Surge
articles.dek: The upcoming epic Ramayana is eyeing a massive opening of around Rs 160 crore worldwide, easily surpassing major blockbusters like Jawan and Animal, though it is expected to stay behind record holders such as RRR and Dhurandhar 2.

p: The cinematic adaptation of Ramayana arrives as a monumental project in the Indian film landscape. Touted as the biggest domestic film ever produced, the feature boasts a massive budget and a wide distribution network spanning global territories.
Industry analysts and trade experts anticipated record-shattering numbers right from the announcement phase, given the sheer scale of production and the prominent star cast attached to the venture.

Global pre-sales officially commenced on Dussehra, giving fans a 15-day window ahead of the scheduled theatrical debut. While overseas markets responded with immediate enthusiasm, ticket sales within India faced initial roadblocks due to business disagreements between exhibitors and distributors regarding revenue sharing.

Most domestic screens kept bookings closed until a few days prior to the premiere. Despite this setback, momentum picked up rapidly during release week, leading to substantial figures by Wednesday morning.
By the final stretch before release, the film accumulated Rs 77 crore in domestic pre-sales for the opening weekend alone, with the opening day contributing roughly Rs 33 crore of that total.

On the international front, pre-sales reached $5.6 million, which included $1.5 million from paid previews in North America. Combined, the global advance collection touched Rs 125 crore, establishing a strong foundation for opening day.

Current box office tracking suggests a worldwide opening day collection of approximately Rs 160 crore gross. While conservative estimates hover around Rs 150 crore, some optimistic projections lean closer to the Rs 200-crore mark.

The Hindi version is expected to drive the domestic earnings significantly, contributing an estimated Rs 55 to 60 crore net, whereas the Kannada version is tracking at more moderate levels despite the presence of star actor Yash.

Even with a projected Rs 160-crore start and a massive release across 70,000 screens distributed by Sony, the film may fall short of the highest-grossing opening days in Indian cinema history. All-time leaders like Pushpa 2, RRR, and Baahubali 2 hold higher opening records.
Furthermore, the feature is expected to trail Dhurandhar 2 and Kalki 2898 AD, while potentially landing ahead of KGF Chapter 2 on the opening-day charts.

Despite missing the top tier of all-time records, the film is poised to comfortably outpace earlier high-profile releases. It will easily eclipse the opening collections of the previous adaptation Adipurush.
It is also projected to dwarf the opening-day numbers of notable Bollywood hits such as Shah Rukh Khan's Jawan and Ranbir Kapoor's previous blockbuster Animal.

Produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios alongside DNEG and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, the epic is directed by Nitesh Tiwari. The stellar cast features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman.
The first installment is slated for a worldwide release on November 5, 2026, with the second part scheduled to arrive during Diwali 2028.

Ramayana is projected to secure a massive worldwide opening day of approximately Rs 160 crore, fueled by strong global pre-sales and a massive international release footprint. Although it will comfortably surpass previous hits like Jawan, Animal, and Adipurush, it is not expected to break the all-time opening records held by films such as RRR and Dhurandhar 2.

facts: Ramayana global advance booking reached Rs 125 crore.
The film is projected to start with Rs 160 crore.
Sony is distributing the film across 70,000 screens worldwide.

Part 2 is set for Diwali 2028.
